records.name: Adapted Birding (PA Center for Adapted Sports)
records.summary: A birding program for people with disabilities, run by the Pennsylvania Center for Adapted Sports. Each outing visits a park or nature site in the region, mostly on paved or firm paths, and every outing needs its own registration.
records.what_you_do: Register for an outing, complete the waiver and forms if you are new, then walk the trail with the group and look for birds.

schedule.text: Outings are scheduled on weekend days in the fall, most starting in the morning, and each one has its own sign-up.

locations.label: Accessible parks in Montgomery, Bucks and Delaware counties

cost.text: The outing pages do not list a fee.

access.notes: Most listed sites have accessible restrooms. Paths vary: some are paved and flat, while others have gravel lots, steep grades, or grassy sections, and some sites have little shade. The Chanticleer outing page advises manual wheelchair users to bring a helper for the steep sections.

first_step.how: Fill in the birding sign-up form for an outing on the program page. First-time participants then hear from the team about waivers and paperwork.
first_step.basis: Any member of the public can register for an outing through a form, and the page explains the first-time paperwork. It does not say beginners are welcome, and space is limited.
first_step.what_to_expect: Outings are group walks on park and nature trails, mostly on weekend mornings. Before your first outing you sign the waivers and paperwork, and the team contacts you after you register. The pages do not list the fee or how long a walk lasts, so ask when you sign up.
first_visit_tips: Register for each outing on its own, since some park outings need a second sign-up with the partner site.
Ask where to meet, because some outings send the meeting spot by email after you register.
Bring sun protection and bug spray, since some sites have little shade and at least one can be buggy.
If you use a manual wheelchair and the trail has steep sections, plan on a helper, as the group advises for one site.

records.notes: Outing pages list each date on its own and do not say the outings repeat, so recurring is set to false. No email is published; the contact page uses a form. The eligibility document linked from the site could not be read, so no eligibility rule was added. Peace Valley and Little Sit outings need separate registration. The site has no FAQ or accessibility page beyond the outing notes.

records.name: Adult Education Philadelphia (volunteer tutors)
records.summary: The city's adult education program, run with community partners. It trains volunteer tutors to help adults build reading, writing, math, computer, and English skills.
records.what_you_do: Tutors work one-on-one with a learner or serve as classroom aides in reading, writing, math, basic computer skills, or English. Tutors take a free training before they are matched with a learner.

schedule.text: Free tutor training of about 10 to 12 hours comes before the first learner match. Tutoring times are set with each learner.

first_step.how: Apply through the online volunteer form linked on the city's adult education page, then email adultedu@phila.gov with any questions.
first_step.basis: There is a clear public application path, and training comes before any learner is matched. The page does not say how long a match takes or what screening applies.
first_step.what_to_expect: You take a free training of about 10 to 12 hours, hosted by subject experts, before you are matched with a learner. After matching, the education provider supports you and offers ongoing professional development. The page does not say how much time each week a tutor gives or whether sessions are in person or online, so ask before you apply.
first_visit_tips: Email adultedu@phila.gov to ask when the next tutor training starts.
Plan on the full 10 to 12 hours of training before you meet a learner.

records.notes: The page does not state a minimum age, background check, clearances, or weekly time commitment. Minimum age 16 is carried over from tier 1 and was not confirmed on this pass. The learner hotline, (833) 750-5627, is for enrolling in classes rather than for tutors, so it is not listed as a contact here. Dated items on the page: an instructor pathway post and a learner GED post from August 2026 (not tutor items), and a volunteer post dated December 31, 2024. The Free Library adult education link on the page is a learner resource and was not checked.

records.name: AFP Greater Philadelphia Chapter
records.summary: The Greater Philadelphia chapter of the fundraising professionals association. It holds coffee talks, workshops and a yearly National Philanthropy Day event.
records.what_you_do: Attend a coffee conversation, join a virtual fundraising workshop, or go to the yearly philanthropy event.

schedule.text: The chapter posts morning coffee talks, virtual workshops, evening dinner events, and a yearly National Philanthropy Day event. Dates change, so check the events page.

locations.label: Coffee conversations at Glenmede and RSM offices, in the suburbs and in Philadelphia
Evening event at The Logan Hotel
The Bellevue Hotel, site of the 2026 National Philanthropy Day

cost.text: Professional membership dues are $320 plus $125 in local chapter dues. Event prices for members and non-members are not shown on the pages read.

first_step.how: Pick an event on the chapter's events page and use its Register link. If you are not sure a non-member can attend, ask through the chapter's contact form first.
first_step.basis: Events are listed publicly with registration links, but the pages do not say how a non-member signs up or whether a first-time guest is welcome. Membership needs a fundraising role, and joining runs through the national association.
first_step.what_to_expect: Coffee talks run from about 8:45 to 10 am at office sites, in the suburbs or in Philadelphia, and last about 75 minutes. Virtual workshops run about an hour over Zoom at midday. Evening events are held at hotels in Center City. Event prices are not shown, so check the registration page before you sign up.
first_visit_tips: Check the price on the registration page before you sign up, since the pages do not show non-member prices.
Ask the chapter whether a non-member can attend before you pay for an event.
The coffee talks in the suburbs need travel outside the city, so check the venue address when you register.
Parking and transit are not listed on the event pages, so check the venue before you go.

records.notes: The events page carried a notice that it is in preview mode and must be published to go live, so confirm the listed events are public before relying on them. Membership: Professional and Associate are $320 plus $125 local dues; Young Professional rates depend on age (26 and under, and 27 to 30); Retired is $75 plus $125 local dues; Organizational dues are not shown. Membership is joined through AFP International, and Professional membership needs direct fundraising responsibility. Volunteering: committees take new members on an ongoing basis through a Committee Interest Form. The page gives no direct form link and no time commitment. The volunteer contact is a board member for volunteer engagement, whose email is hidden on the page, so the chapter phone line is the published route.

records.name: African Cultural Alliance of North America (ACANA)
records.summary: A Philadelphia nonprofit that offers community services, including immigration and legal help, health checks, workforce and construction training, digital skills classes, and youth workshops.
records.what_you_do: Take a class or training, use a legal, benefits, or health service, or join the monthly Wellness check-in on Zoom. Some programs are free, and the site gives no price for most others.

schedule.text: The monthly Wellness check-in is held on Zoom on Wednesday evenings, 5 to 6:30 pm Eastern. Trainings and workshops run as cohorts or on dates posted on the site.

cost.text: Some services are free, including some health screenings and skills training. The site gives no price for most other programs. Legal help is offered pro bono or at a reduced fee.

first_step.how: Call (215) 729-8225 to ask which program fits you, or join the monthly Wednesday evening Zoom Wellness check-in.
first_step.basis: Services are open to residents regardless of background, and the site lists a phone line, an email, and a contact form. It does not say whether beginners get extra help, and office hours are not listed.
first_step.what_to_expect: The Wellness check-in is an online session on Zoom that runs an hour and a half on a Wednesday evening, once a month. Each month covers a different health or life topic. For legal, benefits, or health services, the site does not describe a first visit, so ask the office what happens next.
first_visit_tips: Call ahead, since the site does not list office hours.
For Zoom check-ins, read the newest post, because the meeting ID or QR code changes from month to month.
Ask what to bring for legal or benefits help, since the site does not say.
Ask about cost before you sign up, since most programs do not list a price.

records.notes: Some services are limited to certain people: the Women's Wellness screenings and the Healthy African Woman workshop series are for women, and the workshop series gives access to free or low-cost health services for Philadelphia residents. Legal services are pro bono or reduced fee, and the page says the group has been accredited by the Board of Immigration Appeals since 2011. The health page lists blood pressure, blood sugar, HIV, and BMI checks at the clinic but does not say whether appointments are needed. The opportunities page shows no open positions, only a donation option. The October 16 construction open house is at 5521 Chester Avenue, not the main office; dated events are left out of schedule text. Africatown (philaafricatown.org) runs the skills training and business help that ACANA's site credits to it. It is dropped from leads_only because it is a separate organization outside this batch, and it was not fetched in this pass.

records.name: Al-Bustan Seeds of Culture
records.summary: An Arab arts and language group in Philadelphia. It runs after-school art and drumming for students, Arabic classes for kids and adults, and gallery shows on the second Thursday of each month.
records.what_you_do: Take an Arabic class, come to a gallery exhibition, volunteer through the group's volunteer page, or join arts programming for students.

schedule.text: Open Gallery runs on the second Thursday of each month, 6 to 8 pm. Gallery hours are Tuesday to Friday, 10 am to 6 pm. A monthly games and community afternoon (Finjan Fil-Bustan) falls on a Friday near the end of the month. Adult and kids Arabic courses run in 10 and 15 week terms.

cost.text: Adult Arabic courses cost $400 for Beginner I and II, $480 for Intermediate, and $600 for Beginner III, per 10 week course. Kids' Arabic is $550 per 15 week semester. Gallery and event prices are not shown.

first_step.how: If you are new to Arabic, register for Beginner I on the adult courses page, which meets Monday and Wednesday evenings on Zoom. To see the work first, come to Open Gallery on a second Thursday.
first_step.basis: The adult and kids courses name a beginner level as the starting point and explain how to register. A placement test is needed only above Beginner I, and the gallery is open to visitors on second Thursdays.
first_step.what_to_expect: Adult beginner courses meet live on Zoom on Monday and Wednesday evenings from 6 to 7 pm, for 10 weeks, with about three hours of study outside class for each course. Open Gallery is an evening open house from 6 to 8 pm on the second Thursday, and visitors can attend in person. Course prices are per term, so check the course page before you sign up.
first_visit_tips: Set up Zoom and Google Classroom before the first class, since the course uses both.
Email arabic@albustanseeds.org to confirm start dates, since the course pages do not list term dates.
Plan to buy the textbook separately, and check its price before the course starts, since the page does not show it.
Plan to arrive early on gallery evenings, which run 6 to 8 pm.

records.notes: The adult courses page at /courses returned 404 on the www host; the adult course listing is at /courses-1. Kids' Arabic is for ages 4 to 17, with a Preparatory 1 level for brand-new learners. A $10 skill-level assessment is offered to families unsure of their child's level; the page does not require it. Adult students who finish Beginner I and II get 50 percent off Beginner III. Volunteer page: volunteers can earn community service hours and letters of recommendation on request. The page does not say a service-hours letter is issued, so that field stays unknown. The events page lists April to November 2026 events with no prices; Second Thursdays Open Gallery is listed for October 8 and November 12. Partners named on the events page (Cinema Etcetera, a South Kensington gallery group, and a venue called the Pageant) were not checked; Cinema Etcetera is in leads_only.

records.name: Allens Lane Art Center
records.summary: An art center in Mount Airy with classes for kids ages 5 to 12, for teens, and for adults. It also runs summer camps, a pottery program, and gallery shows with artist talks.
records.what_you_do: Sign up for a semester class, send a child to camp, or come to an opening or artist talk.

schedule.text: Classes run in seasonal terms, with kids' classes listed separately from adult classes. Summer camp is a separate program.

cost.text: Class tuition is not shown on the pages we could read. The site describes its programs as low-cost. Members get tuition discounts on workshops.

first_step.how: Call (215) 248-0546 or email info@allenslane.org to ask which fall classes are open, then register for one online.
first_step.basis: Classes are open to the public with online sign-up, and phone and email are listed for questions. The adult class page showed no upcoming classes when it was read, so confirm before you register.
first_step.what_to_expect: Adult and youth classes run in seasonal terms, and sign-up is online. The pages we read do not show how many weeks a class runs, the class times, or whether materials are included, so ask the center before you register. Kids' classes are listed separately from adult classes.
first_visit_tips: Ask whether the class you want has openings, since the adult class page showed none when it was read.
Ask about scholarships or per-week discounts, since class scholarships are not listed on the pages read.
Ask whether membership makes sense if you plan to take several classes, since members get tuition discounts on workshops.
The office is at 601 W Allens Lane and is open Monday to Thursday, 10 am to 5 pm.

records.notes: Conflict: the home page says Fall 2026 classes began September 8 with registration open, but the adult classes page shows no upcoming classes. The class listings sit on a separate registration site (canvas.allenslane.org) that refused every request, so class times, number of weeks, and class prices were not read. The 2026 pricing a search turned up was for summer camp. Older adult ceramics prices from several years ago were not used. A search snippet mentions partial, need-based scholarships for summer camp; none are listed for classes. Confidence is medium for these reasons.
